Limpid

/LIM-pid/ - the stress falls on LIM · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Limpid means clear, transparent.

The portrait's limpid green eyes seem lit from behind, and visitors swear they follow you.

Worked Example

Reviewers keep praising the translator's limpid English: sentences you look straight through to the meaning, with nothing clouded and nothing showing off.

Limpid is stronger than plain 'clear' because it suggests a beautiful, effortless transparency — the quality of spring water carried over to eyes, air, voices, or prose. Writing can be clear yet clumsy; limpid writing is clear the way still water is.

How Limpid Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

crystalline

crystalline: clear as cut crystal — a close twin

glassy

glassy: smooth and still as glass — about the surface, not what is beneath

Antonyms

murky

murky: so clouded nothing shows through

turbid

turbid: stirred thick with sediment

How Strong Is It? — clean → clear → limpid

clean vs. limpid

clean vs. limpid: Clean means free of dirt but says nothing about seeing through; it stops well short of limpid.

clear vs. limpid

clear vs. limpid: Clear goes further than clean, yet stops short of limpid, which is so transparent it hardly seems to be there.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — limp-

Root — limp-: clear water (Latin limpa)

Suffix — -id

Suffix — -id: adjective ending: having the quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Limp- (clear water) + -id (having the quality of) = having the quality of clear water. Latin limpa named water at its purest, and limpid still measures everything — a pool, a gaze, a paragraph — against that standard of perfect see-through calm.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: Latin limpa may be a cousin of lympha, the clear-water word behind 'lymph,' but scholars call that link only probable — and no other common English word grew from limp- itself. So limpid stands essentially alone, one word holding the root's whole clear stream.

Strength Check

Word Choice

literary

Limpid flatters whatever it touches — water, eyes, a singing tone, prose — by making clarity beautiful. Don't confuse it with limp (drooping); the two are unrelated. And keep it apart from this unit's manifest: limpid describes the medium you see through, manifest the fact that stands in plain view.
